paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Zion looked at the rubble and said, "The LORD has forsaken me; the Lord has forgotten me!" (Isaiah 49:14). I know that feeling. I've been stuck in the dark thinking nobody remembered me. But the LORD doesn't argue with her feelings. He answers with something bigger: "Even if she could forget, I will not forget you!" (Isaiah 49:15).

Then He says, "I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands" (Isaiah 49:16). Palms, friend! That's not a sticky note on the fridge, that's where He looks every time He reaches for anything. The LORD says it isn't only Zion who will see it: "Then all mankind will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob" (Isaiah 49:26). I think that's the part to hold onto: He keeps His people, and He's the one who brings the rescue.

So when you feel forgotten, baker, don't believe the feeling over the promise. Wait on Him, because "those who hope in Me will never be put to shame" (Isaiah 49:23). And since the same God who spoke this to Zion is the one who sent an angel to a junk drawer for me, I'll tell you plain: He knows right where you are. That's why my ovens stay warm, and this story isn't over.
